_comment: Live appearance for the dictionary popup (SUPER+CTRL+D).
Read on every lookup, so a change here takes effect on the NEXT POPUP —
no hms, no reload. Same idea as caelestia/hypr-vars.lua: this file is an
out-of-store symlink, so the live file IS this repo file.
Only the keys present here override; everything else comes from
themeDefaults in modules/home-manager/desktop/dictionary/default.nix.
Delete a key to go back to its default. Invalid JSON is ignored with a
note in $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/dict-popup/last-run.log, so a typo cannot stop
the popup from opening.
Colours are #RRGGBBAA — CSS order, alpha last.
SIZE: fontPx is the one to change. Everything scales off it — the indent
ladder is in em, the headword is 120% of it, and the truncation budget
is maxLines x fontPx x lineHeightPct. width/height are the card in
logical pixels; the popup clamps itself to the usable area, so a size
larger than the screen is pinned rather than cut off.
Keys: width height radius padding borderWidth background border
foreground muted faint rule accent section
fontPx sectionFontPx fontFamily
shadowEnabled shadowColor shadowBlur shadowOffsetY shadowOpacity
shadowPad offsetY margin maxLines
maxLines caps how many lines each dictionary shows before a blue "more"
appears; click it to expand that one dictionary. 0 shows everything.
It is a line BUDGET, not a sense count -- the headword renders larger
than the body text, so 9 lines is roughly a headword plus four or five
lines of definition. macOS truncates the same way, geometrically: it
cuts mid-token ("... | [with  more").
Two things are NOT here because the popup does not draw them: the
background blur is a Hyprland layer_rule (needs hms + hyprctl reload),
and the terminal backend ignores everything but the geometry.
ONE COUPLING TO KNOW ABOUT: popup.blurIgnoreAlpha (a Nix option, 0.7)
is the alpha below which Hyprland does not blur behind the popup. It
has to stay ABOVE shadowColor's alpha and AT OR BELOW background's.
Set it too low and the blur spreads across the shadow pad, which shows
up as a second lighter rounded rectangle outside the card -- it looks
like a frame but it is blur bleeding past the card. Too high and the
card stops being blurred at all. So if you lower background's alpha
below 0.7 here, lower blurIgnoreAlpha to match (that one needs hms).
LIGHT PRESET — macOS's own popup is a light frosted panel, so for the
closest match to Dictionary.app paste these over the keys below:
"background":  "#F2F2F4D8",
"foreground":  "#1A1A1AFF",
"muted":       "#5A5A5AFF",
"faint":       "#7A7A7AFF",
"rule":        "#C8C8C8FF",
"accent":      "#0A64D0FF",
"section":     "#3A3A3AFF",
"shadowColor": "#00000055"
One thing macOS does that this cannot: it runs the section rule inline,
to the right of the name ("English \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500"). Qt's rich text has no
shrink-to-fit table cell and no way to measure text, so the rule goes
under the name instead. See section_heading() in render.py for what was
tried.
